extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy (Plato/Republic)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive criteria for selecting and educating the ideal State's guardians: which studies to teach, what order and spirit of learning to require, and what moral/intellectual qualities the rulers must have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers should be reluctant to govern
rubrics_metrics.description: The State in which the rulers are most reluctant to govern is always the best and most quietly governed; eagerness to govern indicates a worse State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers ought to take office as a stern necessity, not out of love of power or ambition; reluctance to rule is a positive quality in ensuring good governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be just men who accept office from duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians will be just men who take office as a stern necessity and not after the fashion of present rulers seeking private advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and training should ensure they are motivated by justice and duty rather than personal gain, to avoid civil and domestic broils that ruin the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: State must provide a better life than politics
rubrics_metrics.description: You must contrive for your future rulers another and a better life than that of a ruler, so they will not seek office for private advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only if the State offers a life 'richer' in virtue and wisdom than political power will truly fit rulers rule; material rewards must not be the chief attraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers should be 'rich' in virtue and wisdom, not wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: They must be truly rich, not in silver and gold, but in virtue and wisdom, which are the true blessings of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate and prize moral and intellectual goods above material wealth when selecting and honouring rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Those who govern ought not be lovers of the task
rubrics_metrics.description: If rulers are lovers of the task of governing, there will be rival lovers who will fight; hence they should not love ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating incentives that make political office an object of desire or competition among ambitious lovers of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians should be the wisest administrators with other honours
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should be the men who are wisest about affairs of State and by whom the State is best administered, and who at the same time have other honours and another and a better life than that of politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer candidates who already possess other pursuits/honours so that ruling is not their sole aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education must convert the soul from becoming to being
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is the turning round of a soul passing from a day little better than night to the true day of being — the ascent from below which is true philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose studies and pedagogical aims that draw the soul toward the contemplation of eternal truth rather than merely training for practical or opinion-based skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select knowledge that attracts intellect by presenting contradictions to sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The kind of knowledge which invites thought is that in which the senses give contradictory intimations (e.g., unity appearing as one and many), thereby compelling calculation and intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach subjects that provoke intellectual perplexity and require abstract reasoning rather than subjects fully settled by sense-perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic/number is fundamental and double-purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and calculation (arithmetic) are universally applicable and necessary for all arts and sciences; they draw the soul towards being and are useful in war (troop array).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make arithmetic a required subject taught until numbers are seen by mind alone; discourage treating it as mere commercial skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic must be pursued for its philosophical end, not commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Arithmetic should be learned not as merchants or retail-traders but for military use and 'of the soul' — to pass from becoming to truth and being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize abstract, pure reasoning in arithmetic; teachers should repel introducing visible/tangible objects into argument and preserve unity of number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry is required beyond practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometry, beyond the little practical part needed for war, aims at knowledge of the eternal rather than transient applications; if geometry compels us to view being, it concerns the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach geometry to lead the mind toward contemplation of eternal forms; patronize and sequence it properly (plane, solids, then solids in revolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomy should be studied as a path to higher knowledge, not mere observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Astronomy, when rightly pursued, compels the soul to look upwards and should be used to apprehend true motions (absolute swiftness/slowness) by reason, not to slavishly measure visible proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the visible heavens as patterns pointing to higher rational truths; avoid taking the material proportions as eternal or overinvesting in empirical exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studies must follow a correct order and receive State patronage
rubrics_metrics.description: The sciences should be presented in a natural and pedagogically correct sequence (e.g., arithmetic → geometry → solids → astronomy → dialectic); State encouragement and directors are necessary for their flourishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State should honor and direct studies to create continuous earnest search; otherwise difficult branches will remain neglected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony/music must ascend from practice to number-problem study
rubrics_metrics.description: Music (harmony) as practiced often studies heard consonances but fails to reach problems of natural number harmonies; rightly pursued, it can draw the soul upward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage harmonic study that seeks the natural harmonies of number and inter-communion with other mathematical studies, pursued for beauty and the good rather than technical tinkering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical sciences are preparatory, not ultimate; dialectic is supreme
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical sciences 'dream about being' but cannot behold the waking reality so long as they leave hypotheses unexamined; dialectic alone goes directly to first principles and does away with hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, harmony as handmaids to dialectic: necessary preparation but subordinate to dialectical inquiry that reaches the idea of the good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectic is the coping-stone of the sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialectic is of the intellect only and, when pursued by pure intelligence, leads to the perception of the absolute good; no other science can be placed higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require dialectic as the culminating discipline; it lifts the eye of the soul, examines first principles, and must be taught only after prior mathematical preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialectical skill: ability to ask and answer questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should enable rulers to attain the greatest skill in asking and answering questions; this capacity is essential for guardians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include training in dialectical interrogation and rebuttal — readiness to disprove objections not by appeals to opinion but to absolute truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-communication of studies is essential
rubrics_metrics.description: When the studies reach the point of inter-communion and mutual affinities, the pursuit of them has value for the State; otherwise there is no profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curriculum so the mathematical and musical sciences interconnect and feed into dialectic, rather than remaining isolated technical exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must be both warrior and philosopher
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardian is both warrior and philosopher; hence the required knowledge must have a double use — military and philosophical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that subjects selected serve practical military needs (e.g., number for troop arrays, geometry for camps) while simultaneously cultivating the soul toward truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select candidates with natural gifts for arduous study
rubrics_metrics.description: Those to be assigned these studies should have natural gifts: keenness, quick powers of acquisition, good memory, unwearied solid temper, lover of labour; mind more often faints from severity than body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer youth with strong mental stamina and appetite for learning; avoid candidates who are half-industrious or have divided vocations that prevent sustained intellectual toil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject 'bastard' votaries of philosophy — require true vocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy's true sons should take her by the hand, not bastards; votaries should not be half-industrious or have conflicting loves (e.g., love of gymnastic but hate of learning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen out those with lameness in truthfulness, temperance, courage, magnificence, or other virtues; a ruler defective in any virtue is 'lame' and unsuitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral soundness of pupils is crucial
rubrics_metrics.description: Only if those introduced to this system are sound in body and mind will justice have nothing to say against the education; otherwise the scheme will backfire and increase ridicule of philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully consider temperamental and moral qualities during selection; the State must avoid admitting those who will pervert the training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Youth is the time for extraordinary intellectual toil
rubrics_metrics.description: Solon erred in saying old men may learn many things; youth is the time for extraordinary toil and for presenting calculation, geometry and other elements of instruction as preparation for dialectic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin mathematical and preparatory studies in childhood, but do so without coercion — a freeman ought not to be a slave in acquisition of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid instrumental or commercial motives in study
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies must not be pursued as merchants or with view to buying or selling; they must be pursued in the spirit of the philosopher and for the beautiful and good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster motives of love of truth and the soul's good rather than practical profit or vocational advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical training sharpens general apprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Those with natural talent for calculation are generally quick at other knowledge; even the dull, if trained arithmetically, become quicker than otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mathematical training as general intellectual discipline because it compels abstract reasoning and repels reliance on the senses.
